title: Reading the field — and your place in it
objective: Explain how to track a fast-moving field and where the pancreas project fits.

steps.title: Staying current
steps.body: A moving field is followed through reviews (the map), new primary papers (the edges), and preprints (the bleeding edge). In this app, the **Field Pulse** feed surfaces recent, DOI-checked papers so A10/B9 stay current without hard-coding today's news into lessons.

steps.prompt: What's the role of a review paper when learning a field?
options: It's the map — it synthesizes what's known and flags open questions
It's the newest possible result, running ahead of all other papers
It fully replaces any need to ever read the primary papers yourself
It reports the authors' own new experiments on the topic
steps.explanation: Reviews orient you and point to open questions, but they lag the newest primary work — so you pair them with recent papers (and preprints) for the edges.

variants.setup: You're new to a field and want orientation plus open questions.
variants.reveal: A review maps the field and flags open questions; pair it with recent primaries.

steps.setup: The gut DRG-afferent map is advancing fast, but the pancreas is barely charted.
steps.prompt: Where does your project sit in the field?
options: It extends a proven approach to an organ the field hasn't mapped yet
It merely repeats work that was already finished on the pancreas
It abandons the whole DRG approach in favor of something else
It only re-describes the colon that has already been mapped
steps.reveal: Taking the colon playbook — genetic subtypes, viral tools, chemogenetics — to the pancreas puts your project right at an unmapped edge of the field. That's the whole arc of this app: the tracks exist to get you fluent in exactly this.

variants.prompt: The pancreas DREADD project sits in the field as…
options: Extending a proven approach to an unmapped organ
A repeat of work already finished on the pancreas
A rejection of the established DRG approach entirely
variants.explanation: It applies the established toolkit to an organ the field hasn't charted.

sources.note: Review mapping the open questions in spinal sensory innervation of the gut.

reviewNotes: Following the field; Field Pulse; the pancreas gap = the project. Caps Track A.
